A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAT study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching; v3 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training, efficiency, downstream evaluation, fine-tuning, retrieval, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original RAT training, efficiency, downstream, retrieval, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: The intra-chunk recurrence, inter-chunk attention, gating, positional encoding, and SWA hybrid remain unchanged. Equations (1)–(3) and both implementation listings retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain PG19, FineWeb-Edu, the same commonsense and LongBench tasks, and NarrativeQA/QMSum/WikiSum fine-tuning. Table 6 and Appendix C.3 retain eight reported RULER configurations, despite the nine-task wording in both main texts.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the main evaluations and supplementary comparisons, including the reversed design, FLASH, and RNN–dilated attention. Newly cited Hymba is not added to any reported comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 replaces the stated 1.3B setup of primarily 4K training plus additional 16K-context experiments with a 4096-token setup, removing the associated RoPE-base exception of 500,000. This revises the reported settings without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The parameter-allocation and positional-encoding ablations, reversed-design comparisons, FLASH and dilated-attention analyses, length extrapolation, and retrieval analyses are retained with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly discloses repeated preliminary runs and explains the omission of error bars and significance tests. It provides no run counts, seeds, or quantitative uncertainty estimates and does not establish additional runs between versions.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–14 and plotted results in Figures 2–5 are unchanged. The only added qualitative empirical finding is checklist item 7's unquantified statement that preliminary repeated runs showed limited variance.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and computational-complexity reasoning are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs accompany the checklist.

C1.justification: The claims about RAT's intermediate architecture, efficiency–accuracy trade-off, retrieval capability, and complementary SWA hybrid remain intact. Abstract wording changes do not materially alter their scope.

C2.justification: The checklist newly explains why statistical uncertainty is not reported and states that release safeguards are absent because model/data release is outside the current focus. Existing mechanism explanations and the limitations in Section 6 and Appendix C remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 removes the 16K-context configuration and its RoPE base of 500,000 from the implementation documentation. The remaining pseudocode, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds citations to the already listed Samba and newly added Hymba when discussing hybrid architectures. The substantive positioning against earlier methods otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 inserts a standard NeurIPS checklist before Appendix A, updates the publication footer, makes scattered wording edits, and corrects the computation-flow reference from Figure 1a to Figure 1b. The research narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The existing figures and table structures are retained. Tables 8–10 clarify 'Single layer' as 'Single temporal-mixing layer'; checklist insertion and text reflow alter pagination without substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: The corrected Figure 1b reference, clearer latency-table captions, and explicit statistical-reporting disclosure modestly improve clarity and transparency while preserving the scientific evidence. The unexplained removal of the 16K/RoPE configuration leaves some documentation ambiguity, but no identifiable result entries disappear; the overall gains are limited.
